caveats: OLS on ln(horizon); rows beyond the 16h suite ceiling excluded; CI from the slope standard error.
description: Log-linear fit of the 50% horizon against release date, 2024 onward; doubling time in days with a 95% CI. The most recent window, matching METR's own "since 2024" figure.
name: METR horizon doubling times, both windows and both reliability levels
question: How fast is the time horizon doubling, and does the answer depend on the window?
sql: python: fits.loglinear(since=2024-01-01)

caveats: Two points per model on METR's suite; the constant-hazard model is a null, not a claim.
description: How far the observed 50%/80% horizon ratio departs from the constant-hazard (Ord half-life) prediction of ln(0.5)/ln(0.8) = 3.11: the ratio divided by 3.11, per model.
name: Constant-hazard misfit
question: Do the 50% and 80% horizons sit where a constant task-length hazard predicts?
sql:
SELECT a.as_of_date, a.subject AS model, (a.value_numeric / b.value_numeric) / 3.1063 AS value, [a.id, b.id] AS obs_ids
FROM observations a JOIN observations b ON a.subject = b.subject AND a.as_of_date = b.as_of_date
WHERE a.series_key LIKE 'metr.%.horizon_50.pt' AND b.series_key LIKE 'metr.%.horizon_80.pt' AND NOT coalesce(a.disputed, false)

caveats: Fiscal quarters mapped to the calendar quarter of their period end; a fiscal Q4 is the full year minus three quarters. Chips are whole-company, so they include gaming and client chips. Only quarters with all five inputs are kept. The lab estimate uses the run-rate as of the quarter's end (never a later one), and the margin of the year containing the quarter, else the latest earlier year; revenue minus inference compute overstates true gross margin.
description: Each layer's share of the stack's gross profit per calendar quarter. Chips = NVIDIA and AMD whole-company gross profit (filed); cloud = Microsoft Intelligent Cloud revenue minus its cost of revenue (filed, the one cloud segment that files cost); labs = OpenAI and Anthropic, estimated as the run-rate at the quarter's end over four times Epoch's revenue-minus-inference margin for that year (grade C). Apps are unmeasured.
name: Gross profit by layer
question: What share of the stack's gross profit do the labs take, counting them as an estimate?
sql:
WITH gq AS (
  SELECT subject, as_of_date, period_start, value_numeric AS v, [id] AS ids FROM observations
  WHERE series_key IN ('sec.nvda.gross_profit.q', 'sec.amd.gross_profit.q')
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 'msft_ic', r.as_of_date, r.period_start, r.value_numeric - c.value_numeric, [r.id, c.id]
  FROM observations r JOIN observations c ON c.series_key = 'sec_seg.msft.intelligent_cloud.cost_of_revenue.q'
       AND c.as_of_date = r.as_of_date AND c.period_start = r.period_start
  WHERE r.series_key = 'sec_seg.msft.intelligent_cloud.revenue.q'),
gfy AS (
  SELECT subject, as_of_date, period_start, value_numeric AS v, [id] AS ids FROM observations
  WHERE series_key IN ('sec.nvda.gross_profit.fy', 'sec.amd.gross_profit.fy')
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 'msft_ic', r.as_of_date, r.period_start, r.value_numeric - c.value_numeric, [r.id, c.id]
  FROM observations r JOIN observations c ON c.series_key = 'sec_seg.msft.intelligent_cloud.cost_of_revenue.fy'
       AND c.as_of_date = r.as_of_date AND c.period_start = r.period_start
  WHERE r.series_key = 'sec_seg.msft.intelligent_cloud.revenue.fy'),
fill AS (  -- a fiscal Q4 filed only inside the 10-K: full year minus the three quarters inside it
  SELECT f.subject, f.as_of_date, f.v - sum(q.v) AS v, flatten(list_prepend(f.ids, list(q.ids))) AS ids
  FROM gfy f JOIN gq q ON q.subject = f.subject AND q.as_of_date > f.period_start AND q.as_of_date < f.as_of_date
  GROUP BY f.subject, f.as_of_date, f.v, f.ids
  HAVING count(*) = 3 AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM gq q2 WHERE q2.subject = f.subject AND q2.as_of_date = f.as_of_date)),
filed AS (
  SELECT date_trunc('quarter', as_of_date) AS cq, subject, v, ids,
         CASE WHEN subject = 'msft_ic' THEN 'compute_cloud' ELSE 'compute_semis' END AS layer_id
  FROM (SELECT subject, as_of_date, v, ids FROM gq UNION ALL SELECT subject, as_of_date, v, ids FROM fill)),
qs AS (SELECT cq FROM filed GROUP BY cq HAVING count(DISTINCT subject) = 3),
margin AS (  -- Epoch's full-year revenue minus inference compute, over revenue
  SELECT r.subject, year(r.as_of_date) AS fy, 1 - i.value_numeric / r.value_numeric AS m, [r.id, i.id] AS ids
  FROM observations r JOIN observations i ON i.subject = r.subject AND i.as_of_date = r.as_of_date
       AND i.series_key = 'epoch.' || r.subject || '.inference_compute_usd.fy'
  WHERE r.series_key IN ('epoch.openai.revenue_usd.fy', 'epoch.anthropic.revenue_usd.fy') AND r.value_numeric > 0),
rr AS (SELECT subject, as_of_date, value_numeric AS v, id FROM observations
       WHERE series_key IN ('epoch.openai.revenue_run_rate_usd.pt', 'epoch.anthropic.revenue_run_rate_usd.pt')),
lab AS (  -- the run-rate as of the quarter's end (never a later one) over four, times the year's margin
  SELECT cq, subject, v, ids FROM (
    SELECT qs.cq, rr.subject, rr.v / 4 * margin.m AS v, list_prepend(rr.id, margin.ids) AS ids,
           row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY qs.cq, rr.subject ORDER BY rr.as_of_date DESC, margin.fy DESC) AS rn
    FROM qs JOIN rr ON rr.as_of_date < qs.cq + INTERVAL 3 MONTH AND rr.as_of_date >= qs.cq + INTERVAL 3 MONTH - INTERVAL 183 DAY
            JOIN margin ON margin.subject = rr.subject AND margin.fy <= year(qs.cq))
  WHERE rn = 1),
complete AS (SELECT cq FROM lab GROUP BY cq HAVING count(DISTINCT subject) = 2),
by_layer AS (
  SELECT f.cq, f.layer_id, 'filed' AS basis, sum(f.v) AS gp, flatten(list(f.ids)) AS ids FROM filed f JOIN complete USING (cq) GROUP BY 1, 2
  UNION ALL
  SELECT l.cq, 'model', 'estimated', sum(l.v), flatten(list(l.ids)) FROM lab l JOIN complete USING (cq) GROUP BY 1)
SELECT (cq + INTERVAL 3 MONTH - INTERVAL 1 DAY)::DATE AS as_of_date, layer_id, basis, gp / sum(gp) OVER (PARTITION BY cq) AS value,
       list_distinct(flatten(list(ids) OVER (PARTITION BY cq))) AS obs_ids
FROM by_layer

caveats: Fiscal quarters mapped to the calendar quarter of their period end (NVIDIA's late-July quarter counts as Q3); a filer's unreported fiscal Q4 is filled as fiscal year minus its three reported quarters and cites all four filings; quarters where any of the five segments is still missing are dropped; segment operating income, not gross profit; only two layers so far.
description: Each layer's share of the AI stack's filed segment operating income per calendar quarter. Semis = NVIDIA Compute & Networking + AMD Data Center; cloud = AWS + Google Cloud + Microsoft Intelligent Cloud. Labs and apps join when a filed or estimated series exists.
name: Filed operating income, five segments
question: Where in the stack does filed operating income bulge?
sql:
WITH q AS (
  SELECT subject, series_key, as_of_date, period_start, value_numeric AS v, id
  FROM observations WHERE series_key LIKE 'sec_seg.%.operating_income.q'),
fy AS (
  SELECT subject, replace(series_key, '.fy', '.q') AS series_key, as_of_date, period_start, value_numeric AS v, id
  FROM observations WHERE series_key LIKE 'sec_seg.%.operating_income.fy'),
fill AS (  -- FY minus the three quarters inside it, when exactly three are reported
  SELECT fy.subject, fy.series_key, fy.as_of_date, fy.v - sum(q.v) AS v, list_prepend(fy.id, list(q.id ORDER BY q.id)) AS ids
  FROM fy JOIN q ON q.subject = fy.subject AND q.series_key = fy.series_key
                 AND q.as_of_date > fy.period_start AND q.as_of_date < fy.as_of_date
  GROUP BY fy.subject, fy.series_key, fy.as_of_date, fy.v, fy.id
  HAVING count(*) = 3 AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM q q2 WHERE q2.series_key = fy.series_key AND q2.as_of_date = fy.as_of_date)),
allq AS (
  SELECT subject, as_of_date, v, [id] AS ids FROM q
  UNION ALL SELECT subject, as_of_date, v, ids FROM fill),
seg AS (
  SELECT date_trunc('quarter', as_of_date) AS cq, subject, v, ids,
         CASE WHEN subject IN ('nvda', 'amd') THEN 'compute_semis' ELSE 'compute_cloud' END AS layer_id
  FROM allq),
complete AS (SELECT cq FROM seg GROUP BY cq HAVING count(DISTINCT subject) = 5),
by_layer AS (SELECT s.cq, s.layer_id, sum(v) AS oi, flatten(list(ids)) AS ids FROM seg s JOIN complete c USING (cq) GROUP BY 1, 2)
SELECT (cq + INTERVAL 3 MONTH - INTERVAL 1 DAY)::DATE AS as_of_date, layer_id, oi / sum(oi) OVER (PARTITION BY cq) AS value,
       list_distinct(flatten(list(ids) OVER (PARTITION BY cq))) AS obs_ids
FROM by_layer

caveats: Only covered filers; Broadcom, TSMC, Oracle and the neoclouds are absent, so levels overstate concentration. Fiscal quarters mapped to the calendar quarter of their period end. Ramp lab shares allow multi-homing and are normalised to sum to one.
description: Herfindahl index (sum of squared revenue shares, 0-1) among the filers the tracker covers in a layer, per calendar quarter. Semis = NVIDIA Data Center vs AMD Data Center; cloud = AWS vs Google Cloud vs Microsoft Intelligent Cloud; model = Ramp's share of businesses paying each lab, normalised.
name: Concentration by layer
question: Is any layer fragmenting while its neighbours stay concentrated?
sql:
WITH rev AS (
  SELECT date_trunc('quarter', as_of_date) AS cq, subject, value_numeric AS v, id,
         CASE WHEN subject IN ('nvda', 'amd') THEN 'compute_semis' ELSE 'compute_cloud' END AS layer_id,
         CASE WHEN subject IN ('nvda', 'amd') THEN 2 ELSE 3 END AS need
  FROM observations
  WHERE series_key IN ('sec_seg.nvda.data_center.revenue.q', 'sec_seg.amd.data_center.revenue.q',
                       'sec_seg.amzn.aws.revenue.q', 'sec_seg.googl.cloud.revenue.q', 'sec_seg.msft.intelligent_cloud.revenue.q')),
complete AS (SELECT cq, layer_id FROM rev GROUP BY cq, layer_id, need HAVING count(DISTINCT subject) = need),
sh AS (SELECT (r.cq + INTERVAL 3 MONTH - INTERVAL 1 DAY)::DATE AS as_of_date, r.layer_id,
              r.v / sum(r.v) OVER (PARTITION BY r.cq, r.layer_id) AS s, r.id
       FROM rev r JOIN complete c USING (cq, layer_id)),
lab AS (SELECT as_of_date, 'model' AS layer_id, value_numeric / sum(value_numeric) OVER (PARTITION BY as_of_date) AS s, id
        FROM observations WHERE series_key LIKE 'ramp.%.business_paid_share.m')
SELECT as_of_date, layer_id, sum(s * s) AS value, list(id ORDER BY id) AS obs_ids
FROM (SELECT * FROM sh UNION ALL SELECT * FROM lab) GROUP BY 1, 2

caveats: Tier-5 inputs; excludes debt, compute credits and cloud commitments; run-rates are press-reported annualised months.
description: A lab's latest revenue run-rate divided by the equity it had raised by that date (Epoch data). Above 1 means a year of run-rate exceeds all capital raised.
name: Lab recoupment ratios
question: How much run-rate has each lab earned per dollar of capital raised?
sql:
WITH rr AS (SELECT subject, as_of_date, value_numeric AS rev, id FROM observations WHERE series_key LIKE 'epoch.%.revenue_run_rate_usd.pt'),
     eq AS (SELECT subject, as_of_date, value_numeric AS eq, id FROM observations WHERE series_key LIKE 'epoch.%.round_equity_usd.pt')
SELECT rr.as_of_date, rr.subject AS entity, rr.rev / sum(eq.eq) AS value,
       list_concat([rr.id], list(eq.id ORDER BY eq.id)) AS obs_ids
FROM rr JOIN eq ON eq.subject = rr.subject AND eq.as_of_date <= rr.as_of_date
GROUP BY rr.as_of_date, rr.subject, rr.rev, rr.id

caveats: Different geographies (CA claims vs US employment) and different exposure measures; a count, not a test. Each tracker's latest reading counts, whatever its month.
description: Number of the four monthly labour trackers whose latest reading is past its own AI-attributable-break threshold (0-4), counting each tracker once and none of the entry-level cuts (Appendix B asks for a break beyond entry level). Thresholds - most-exposed quintile employment y/y <= -3% (Canaries, all ages); exposed-vs-unexposed gap <= -10% (Revelio); high-exposure claims 3-month average +5% or more m/m (CAIT, potential exposure, computed from its counts); occupational-mix dissimilarity >= 10 pp (Yale).
name: Labour-tracker concordance
question: Do the four monthly labour trackers agree?
sql:
WITH obs AS (
  SELECT series_key, value_numeric AS v, as_of_date, [id] AS ids FROM observations
  WHERE series_key IN ('canaries.us_exposure_q5.employment_yoy.m', 'revelio.us_exposed.growth_gap.m',
                       'yale_budget_lab_data.us_workers.occupation_dissimilarity_pp.m')),
cait AS (SELECT as_of_date, value_numeric AS v, id FROM observations WHERE series_key = 'cait.ca_top_quartile_potential.claims.m'),
cma AS (SELECT as_of_date, avg(v) OVER w AS ma, count(*) OVER w AS n, list(id) OVER w AS ids
        FROM cait WINDOW w AS (ORDER BY as_of_date ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW)),
cchg AS (SELECT 'cait_3mma_mom' AS series_key, ma / lag(ma) OVER o - 1 AS v, as_of_date,
                list_distinct(list_concat(ids, lag(ids) OVER o)) AS ids, n, lag(n) OVER o AS n0
         FROM cma WINDOW o AS (ORDER BY as_of_date)),
allx AS (SELECT series_key, v, as_of_date, ids FROM obs UNION ALL SELECT series_key, v, as_of_date, ids FROM cchg WHERE n = 3 AND n0 = 3),
latest AS (SELECT *, row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY series_key ORDER BY as_of_date DESC) AS rn FROM allx),
-- a break is that tracker's own fast band, read from the seed rather than restated here
tracker AS (SELECT * FROM (VALUES
    ('canaries.us_exposure_q5.employment_yoy.m', 'canaries_exposed_employment_yoy'),
    ('revelio.us_exposed.growth_gap.m', 'revelio_exposed_vs_unexposed_growth'),
    ('cait_3mma_mom', 'cait_high_exposure_claims'),
    ('yale_budget_lab_data.us_workers.occupation_dissimilarity_pp.m', 'yale_occupational_mix_dissimilarity'))
  AS t(series_key, indicator_id))
SELECT max(l.as_of_date) AS as_of_date,
       sum(CASE WHEN (b.fast_lo IS NULL OR l.v >= b.fast_lo) AND (b.fast_hi IS NULL OR l.v <= b.fast_hi)
                THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)::DOUBLE AS value,
       list_distinct(flatten(list(l.ids))) AS obs_ids
FROM latest l JOIN tracker t USING (series_key) JOIN bands b ON b.indicator_id = t.indicator_id
WHERE l.rn = 1

caveats: Hyperscaler capex is not all AI; the revenue side is run-rates (annualised, press-reported) plus one annual survey and double-counts where enterprises buy from labs; grade C by construction. Most filers report capex only year to date, so fiscal quarters are differenced (six months minus the first quarter, and so on; a fourth quarter is the year minus nine months), and a window counts only when all five filers have four quarters in it.
description: Trailing four quarters of hyperscaler capex (Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon, Meta, Oracle; filed) divided by AI revenue (frontier-lab run-rates from Epoch plus Menlo's enterprise generative-AI spend), at each quarter end.
name: Capex to AI revenue
question: How far ahead of AI revenue is hyperscaler capex running?
sql:
WITH cum AS (  -- year-to-date figures share their fiscal year's start date; a filed three-month quarter stands alone
  SELECT subject, as_of_date, period_start, value_numeric AS v, id FROM observations
  WHERE source_ns = 'sec' AND measure = 'capex' AND grain IN ('q', 'h1', '9m', 'fy')
    AND subject IN ('msft', 'googl', 'amzn', 'meta', 'orcl')),
diffed AS (
  SELECT subject, as_of_date, v - coalesce(lag(v) OVER w, 0) AS v,
         list_filter([id, lag(id) OVER w], x -> x IS NOT NULL) AS ids,
         date_diff('day', coalesce(lag(as_of_date) OVER w, period_start), as_of_date) AS days
  FROM cum WINDOW w AS (PARTITION BY subject, period_start ORDER BY as_of_date)),
capex AS (  -- one figure per fiscal quarter; a filed quarter beats a differenced one
  SELECT date_trunc('quarter', as_of_date) AS cq, subject, v, ids FROM diffed WHERE days BETWEEN 80 AND 100
  QUALIFY row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY subject, as_of_date ORDER BY len(ids), ids) = 1),
qs AS (SELECT DISTINCT cq FROM capex WHERE cq >= DATE '2024-01-01'),
per AS (
  SELECT q.cq, c.subject, sum(c.v) AS v, flatten(list(c.ids)) AS ids FROM qs q JOIN capex c ON c.cq > q.cq - INTERVAL 12 MONTH AND c.cq <= q.cq
  GROUP BY q.cq, c.subject HAVING count(*) = 4),
capex4 AS (SELECT cq, sum(v) AS v, list_sort(flatten(list(ids))) AS ids FROM per GROUP BY cq HAVING count(*) = 5),
rr AS (SELECT entity_id, as_of_date, value_numeric AS v, id FROM observations WHERE series_key LIKE 'epoch.%.revenue_run_rate_usd.pt' AND entity_id IS NOT NULL),
rr_latest AS (
  SELECT q.cq, r.entity_id, arg_max(r.v, r.as_of_date) AS v, arg_max(r.id, r.as_of_date) AS id FROM qs q JOIN rr r ON r.as_of_date <= q.cq + INTERVAL 3 MONTH AND r.as_of_date > q.cq - INTERVAL 9 MONTH GROUP BY 1, 2),
ent AS (SELECT as_of_date, value_numeric AS v, id FROM observations WHERE series_key = 'menlo.us_enterprise.genai_spend_usd.fy'),
ent_latest AS (SELECT q.cq, arg_max(e.v, e.as_of_date) AS v, arg_max(e.id, e.as_of_date) AS id FROM qs q JOIN ent e ON e.as_of_date <= q.cq + INTERVAL 3 MONTH GROUP BY 1)
SELECT (c.cq + INTERVAL 3 MONTH - INTERVAL 1 DAY)::DATE AS as_of_date,
       c.v / ((SELECT sum(v) FROM rr_latest r WHERE r.cq = c.cq) + e.v) AS value,
       list_distinct(flatten([c.ids, (SELECT list(id) FROM rr_latest r WHERE r.cq = c.cq), [e.id]])) AS obs_ids
FROM capex4 c JOIN ent_latest e USING (cq)

caveats: Mixes instruments (equity, guarantees, commitments) with different risk; "up to" and floor values taken at face; cumulative, so it only rises until a row is superseded.
description: Cumulative signed circular / vendor-financing commitments in USD by quarter - equity stakes, guarantees, take-or-pay contracts and backstops between suppliers and their AI-lab customers - excluding letters of intent, talks and self-reported aggregates.
name: Circular financing total
question: How much circular financing has been signed?
sql:
WITH deals AS (
  SELECT as_of_date, value_numeric AS v, id FROM observations
  WHERE series_key LIKE 'circular.%_usd.pt'
    AND series_key NOT LIKE '%loi_usd%' AND series_key NOT LIKE '%talks_usd%' AND series_key NOT LIKE '%total_commitments%'
    AND series_key NOT LIKE '%commercial_rpo%')
SELECT last_deal AS as_of_date, sum(v) OVER (ORDER BY q_end) AS value,
       flatten(list(ids) OVER (ORDER BY q_end)) AS obs_ids
FROM (SELECT date_trunc('quarter', as_of_date)::DATE AS q_end, max(as_of_date) AS last_deal, sum(v) AS v, list(id ORDER BY id) AS ids
      FROM deals GROUP BY 1)

caveats: List prices on one router, prompt tokens only; the horizon is METR's suite, not general capability; only models present in both datasets count; a price series starts on 10 Sep 2026 and records change points, so the trend needs months; a delisted model's last price carries forward.
description: Cheapest available capability-hour - on each price change date, the minimum over METR-measured models of OpenRouter prompt price (USD per million tokens, each model's latest price carried forward) divided by the model's latest 50% time horizon in hours.
name: Price per capability
question: What does a METR-hour of capability cost on OpenRouter?
sql:
WITH h AS (
  SELECT subject, arg_max(value_numeric, as_of_date) AS minutes, arg_max(id, as_of_date) AS hid
  FROM observations WHERE series_key LIKE 'metr.%.horizon_50.pt' AND NOT coalesce(disputed, false) GROUP BY subject),
p AS (SELECT subject, as_of_date, value_numeric AS usd, id FROM observations WHERE series_key LIKE 'openrouter.%.price_prompt_usd_per_mtok.pt' AND value_numeric > 0),
d AS (SELECT DISTINCT as_of_date FROM p),
cp AS (SELECT d.as_of_date, p.subject, arg_max(p.usd, p.as_of_date) AS usd, arg_max(p.id, p.as_of_date) AS pid
       FROM d JOIN p ON p.as_of_date <= d.as_of_date GROUP BY 1, 2)
, r AS (SELECT cp.as_of_date, min(cp.usd / (h.minutes / 60)) AS value, arg_min([cp.pid, h.hid], cp.usd / (h.minutes / 60)) AS obs_ids
FROM cp JOIN h USING (subject) GROUP BY cp.as_of_date)
SELECT * FROM r QUALIFY value IS DISTINCT FROM lag(value) OVER (ORDER BY as_of_date)  -- change points only

caveats: Filers name customers only by letter or number and rename them each filing, so this is the top share, not one customer tracked over time; indirect sales through distributors and cloud providers are not attributed.
description: The largest direct customer's share of a filer's total revenue per fiscal quarter, from the customer-concentration facts in its 10-Q and 10-K (P1 §6, semis).
name: Top direct customer's share of NVIDIA revenue
question: How dependent is the chip layer's rent on a handful of buyers?
sql:
SELECT as_of_date, subject AS entity, max(value_numeric) AS value, [arg_max(id, value_numeric)] AS obs_ids
FROM observations WHERE series_key LIKE 'sec_seg.%.customer_revenue_share.%.q' GROUP BY as_of_date, subject

caveats: Fiscal years only (quarters are too noisy); whole-company revenue, not AI revenue; skipped when revenue fell. Hyperscalers and CoreWeave.
description: The change in a cloud filer's capital expenditure over the change in its revenue, fiscal year on fiscal year (P1 §6, cloud).
name: Incremental capex to incremental revenue
question: How many new dollars of capex does each new dollar of cloud revenue cost?
sql:
WITH j AS (
  SELECT c.subject, c.as_of_date, c.value_numeric AS capex, r.value_numeric AS rev, [c.id, r.id] AS ids
  FROM observations c JOIN observations r
    ON r.source_ns = 'sec' AND r.subject = c.subject AND r.measure = 'revenue' AND r.grain = 'fy'
   AND r.as_of_date = c.as_of_date
  WHERE c.source_ns = 'sec' AND c.measure = 'capex' AND c.grain = 'fy'
    AND c.subject IN ('msft', 'googl', 'amzn', 'meta', 'orcl', 'crwv')),
p AS (SELECT *, lag(capex) OVER w AS capex0, lag(rev) OVER w AS rev0, lag(ids) OVER w AS ids0, lag(as_of_date) OVER w AS d0
      FROM j WINDOW w AS (PARTITION BY subject ORDER BY as_of_date))
SELECT as_of_date, subject AS entity, (capex - capex0) / (rev - rev0) AS value, list_concat(ids, ids0) AS obs_ids
FROM p WHERE capex0 IS NOT NULL AND rev > rev0 AND date_diff('day', d0, as_of_date) BETWEEN 350 AND 380

caveats: Two graders with different item lists; each counts once, at its latest reading.
description: The mean of the two graders' latest readings of AI 2027's quantitative predictions against what happened (AI Futures Project's own grading and the independent ai2027-tracker), as a share of the predicted pace.
name: Surprise index
question: Is AI 2027 running ahead of or behind its own quantitative predictions, by its graders' reckoning?
sql:
WITH l AS (SELECT series_key, value_numeric AS v, as_of_date, id,
                  row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY series_key ORDER BY as_of_date DESC) AS rn
           FROM observations WHERE series_key IN ('aifutures_blog.ai_2027_quantitative.pace_vs_predicted.pt',
                                                  'ai2027_tracker.ai_2027_quantitative.pace_vs_predicted.pt'))
SELECT max(as_of_date) AS as_of_date, avg(v) AS value, list(id ORDER BY id) AS obs_ids FROM l WHERE rn = 1 HAVING count(*) > 0

caveats: Seed-list entities only, attributed by primary membership; debt excluded.
description: Equity venture dollars over the trailing four calendar quarters at each quarter end, per layer (sublayer_id "all") and per sub-layer.
name: Venture dollars, trailing four quarters
question: How much equity has each layer raised over the past year?
sql:
WITH m AS (SELECT entity_id, layer_id, sublayer_id FROM entity_membership WHERE is_primary AND sublayer_id IS NOT NULL),
r AS (SELECT date_trunc('quarter', v.as_of_date) AS cq, m.layer_id, m.sublayer_id, v.v, v.id
      FROM venture_rounds v JOIN m USING (entity_id) WHERE v.kind = 'equity' AND v.as_of_date >= DATE '2022-04-01'),
qs AS (SELECT DISTINCT cq FROM r WHERE cq >= DATE '2023-01-01'),
w AS (SELECT qs.cq, r.layer_id, r.sublayer_id, r.v, r.id FROM qs JOIN r ON r.cq > qs.cq - INTERVAL 12 MONTH AND r.cq <= qs.cq)
SELECT (cq + INTERVAL 3 MONTH - INTERVAL 1 DAY)::DATE AS as_of_date, layer_id, coalesce(sublayer_id, 'all') AS sublayer_id,
       sum(v) AS value, list(id ORDER BY id) AS obs_ids
FROM w GROUP BY GROUPING SETS ((cq, layer_id), (cq, layer_id, sublayer_id))

caveats: Run-rates are press-reported annualised months (tier 5); rounds are mostly Epoch (tier 5). Other sub-layers have no revenue series outside the labs, so this is measured for frontier labs only.
description: Frontier labs' primary-round dollars over the trailing four calendar quarters divided by their summed latest revenue run-rates at quarter end (v2 §9 venture capital intensity, frontier-lab sub-layer). Only labs with a run-rate on record in the twelve months to quarter end count, on both sides.
name: Venture capital intensity, frontier labs
question: How many dollars of new capital do the frontier labs raise per dollar of run-rate?
sql:
WITH rounds AS (SELECT entity_id, as_of_date, v, id FROM venture_rounds WHERE kind = 'equity'),
labs AS (SELECT entity_id FROM entity_membership WHERE is_primary AND sublayer_id = 'frontier_labs'),
rr AS (SELECT entity_id, as_of_date, value_numeric AS rev, id FROM observations WHERE series_key LIKE 'epoch.%.revenue_run_rate_usd.pt' AND entity_id IN (SELECT entity_id FROM labs)),
qs AS (SELECT DISTINCT date_trunc('quarter', as_of_date) AS cq FROM rounds WHERE as_of_date >= DATE '2023-01-01'),
rev AS (SELECT cq, entity_id, rev, id FROM (
          SELECT qs.cq, rr.*, row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY qs.cq, rr.entity_id ORDER BY rr.as_of_date DESC) AS rn
          FROM qs JOIN rr ON rr.as_of_date < qs.cq + INTERVAL 3 MONTH AND rr.as_of_date >= qs.cq + INTERVAL 3 MONTH - INTERVAL 12 MONTH)
        WHERE rn = 1),
raised AS (SELECT qs.cq, r.entity_id, r.v, r.id FROM qs JOIN rounds r ON date_trunc('quarter', r.as_of_date) > qs.cq - INTERVAL 12 MONTH AND date_trunc('quarter', r.as_of_date) <= qs.cq
           WHERE r.entity_id IN (SELECT entity_id FROM rev WHERE rev.cq = qs.cq))
SELECT (rv.cq + INTERVAL 3 MONTH - INTERVAL 1 DAY)::DATE AS as_of_date,
       (SELECT sum(v) FROM raised WHERE raised.cq = rv.cq) / sum(rv.rev) AS value,
       list_concat((SELECT list(id ORDER BY id) FROM raised WHERE raised.cq = rv.cq), list(rv.id ORDER BY rv.id)) AS obs_ids
FROM rev rv GROUP BY rv.cq HAVING sum(rv.rev) > 0 AND (SELECT sum(v) FROM raised WHERE raised.cq = rv.cq) > 0

caveats: Denominator is the seed list, not the market; frontier rounds are mostly Epoch (tier 5) because the labs raise through vehicles that do not file Form D.
description: Frontier labs' share of all tracked primary-round dollars over the trailing four calendar quarters (P1 §7
name: Frontier share of venture dollars
question: What share of tracked venture dollars goes to the frontier labs?
sql:
WITH rounds AS (SELECT entity_id, as_of_date, v, id FROM venture_rounds WHERE kind = 'equity'),
m AS (SELECT entity_id, sublayer_id FROM entity_membership WHERE is_primary AND sublayer_id IS NOT NULL),
q AS (SELECT date_trunc('quarter', r.as_of_date) AS cq, m.sublayer_id, r.v, r.id FROM rounds r JOIN m USING (entity_id) WHERE r.as_of_date >= DATE '2023-01-01'),
qs AS (SELECT DISTINCT cq FROM q)
SELECT (qs.cq + INTERVAL 3 MONTH - INTERVAL 1 DAY)::DATE AS as_of_date,
       sum(CASE WHEN q.sublayer_id = 'frontier_labs' THEN q.v ELSE 0 END) / sum(q.v) AS value,
       list(q.id ORDER BY q.id) AS obs_ids
FROM qs JOIN q ON q.cq > qs.cq - INTERVAL 12 MONTH AND q.cq <= qs.cq GROUP BY 1 HAVING sum(q.v) > 0

caveats: The index composition changes between Artificial Analysis versions and every model is re-scored on the current version, so the history is today's scores placed at release dates, not what was measured then. Artificial Analysis sometimes moves a model's release date; v3 keeps only each model's most recently retrieved row.
description: Highest Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index among models released on or before each date on which a new record was set (index rows are dated by model release).
name: Frontier Intelligence Index
question: What is the best Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, and when was each record set?
sql:
WITH one AS (SELECT subject, as_of_date, value_numeric, id FROM observations
             WHERE series_key LIKE 'aa.%.intelligence_index.pt' AND NOT coalesce(disputed, false)
             QUALIFY row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY subject ORDER BY retrieved_at DESC, as_of_date DESC, id) = 1),
x AS (SELECT as_of_date, max(value_numeric) AS v, arg_max(id, value_numeric) AS id FROM one GROUP BY 1)
SELECT as_of_date, v AS value, [id] AS obs_ids FROM x QUALIFY v >= max(v) OVER (ORDER BY as_of_date)

caveats: Models are matched on METR's id with its "_inspect" suffix dropped, so only models named alike in both datasets count; list prices; METR's horizon is software tasks under its suite.
description: Cheapest capability-hour on Artificial Analysis prices - on each price change date, the lowest blended price (USD per million tokens, latest price carried forward) divided by the model's latest METR 50% time horizon in hours, across models in both datasets.
name: Price per capability, Artificial Analysis
question: What does a METR-hour cost at Artificial Analysis blended prices, and what does a near-frontier index point cost?
sql:
WITH h AS (SELECT regexp_replace(subject, '_inspect$', '') AS subject, arg_max(value_numeric, as_of_date) AS minutes,
                  arg_max(id, as_of_date) AS hid FROM observations
           WHERE series_key LIKE 'metr.%.horizon_50.pt' AND NOT coalesce(disputed, false) GROUP BY 1),
p AS (SELECT subject, as_of_date, value_numeric AS usd, id FROM observations
      WHERE series_key LIKE 'aa.%.price_blended_usd_per_mtok.pt' AND value_numeric > 0),
d AS (SELECT DISTINCT as_of_date FROM p),
cp AS (SELECT d.as_of_date, p.subject, arg_max(p.usd, p.as_of_date) AS usd, arg_max(p.id, p.as_of_date) AS pid
       FROM d JOIN p ON p.as_of_date <= d.as_of_date GROUP BY 1, 2)
, r AS (SELECT cp.as_of_date, min(cp.usd / (h.minutes / 60)) AS value, arg_min([cp.pid, h.hid], cp.usd / (h.minutes / 60)) AS obs_ids
FROM cp JOIN h USING (subject) GROUP BY 1)
SELECT * FROM r QUALIFY value IS DISTINCT FROM lag(value) OVER (ORDER BY as_of_date)  -- change points only

caveats: Denominator is the seed list, not the market; per sub-layer it is meaningless on current coverage (one to four rounds per cell), so it is computed stack-wide only.
description: Share of tracked primary-round dollars raised by the three largest raisers over the trailing four calendar quarters, across the whole seed list.
name: Top-three share of venture dollars
question: What share of tracked venture dollars do the three largest raisers take?
sql:
-- ponytail: the f/e/rounds/m CTEs are copied from frontier_share_of_venture_dollars; a shared view when a third venture metric needs them
WITH rounds AS (SELECT entity_id, as_of_date, v, id FROM venture_rounds WHERE kind = 'equity'),
m AS (SELECT entity_id FROM entity_membership WHERE is_primary AND sublayer_id IS NOT NULL),
q AS (SELECT date_trunc('quarter', r.as_of_date) AS cq, r.entity_id, r.v, r.id FROM rounds r JOIN m USING (entity_id) WHERE r.as_of_date >= DATE '2023-01-01'),
qs AS (SELECT DISTINCT cq FROM q),
win AS (SELECT qs.cq, q.entity_id, sum(q.v) AS v, list(q.id) AS ids FROM qs JOIN q ON q.cq > qs.cq - INTERVAL 12 MONTH AND q.cq <= qs.cq GROUP BY 1, 2),
rk AS (SELECT *, row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY cq ORDER BY v DESC, entity_id) AS r, sum(v) OVER (PARTITION BY cq) AS tot FROM win)
SELECT (cq + INTERVAL 3 MONTH - INTERVAL 1 DAY)::DATE AS as_of_date, sum(v) FILTER (WHERE r <= 3) / max(tot) AS value,
       flatten(list(ids)) AS obs_ids
FROM rk GROUP BY cq HAVING max(tot) > 0

caveats: One router, and only the models on its public list, over the router's own trailing window. A model entering or leaving the list moves the sum, so the level is a sample and the growth rate is the reading.
description: Tokens routed through OpenRouter to the models on its public rankings, summed across the list, at each snapshot date.
name: Tokens routed through a public router
question: How much AI work is actually being run, and how fast is that growing?
sql:
SELECT as_of_date, sum(value_numeric) AS value, list(id ORDER BY id) AS obs_ids
FROM observations WHERE series_key LIKE 'openrouter_rankings.%.tokens.d' GROUP BY as_of_date

caveats: Scores sit at model release dates, often from runs with no compute limit and from mixed scaffolds; a test that stopped getting rows keeps its old record, which is why each test's newest row is exported beside it. A tie on one date keeps the row with the smallest id. Scores on different tests are not comparable to each other.
description: The running best score on each capability test the site reads, by release date, on each date a new record was set; one row per test per record. Tests are share-valued and higher is better. Epoch's compilations of external results (ARC-AGI-2, CL-bench, APEX-Agents, PostTrainBench, GDPval, the Remote Labor Index and FrontierSWE, plus SciCode and CritPt as Artificial Analysis scores them), Epoch's own FrontierMath Tier 4 runs, and HAL's accuracy for the agents it evaluates. HAL's reliability index is left out, since it is not a share of tasks solved.
name: Best score on real freelance projects
question: What share of real paid freelance projects can the best model complete end to end, and when was that record set?
sql:
WITH pts AS (
  SELECT source_ns || '.' || measure AS test, as_of_date, value_numeric AS v, id FROM observations
  WHERE value_numeric IS NOT NULL AND NOT coalesce(disputed, false) AND grain = 'pt' AND (
    (source_ns = 'epoch_bench' AND measure IN ('arc_agi_2', 'cl_bench', 'apex_agents', 'posttrainbench', 'gdpval', 'rli',
                                               'critpt', 'frontierswe', 'scicode', 'frontiermath_t4'))
    OR (source_ns = 'hal_reliability' AND measure = 'accuracy'))
), d AS (SELECT test, as_of_date, max(v) AS v, list(id ORDER BY v DESC, id)[1] AS id FROM pts GROUP BY 1, 2)
SELECT as_of_date, test, v AS value, [id] AS obs_ids FROM d
QUALIFY v > coalesce(max(v) OVER (PARTITION BY test ORDER BY as_of_date ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND 1 PRECEDING), -1)

caveats: One router with a developer-heavy, price-sensitive mix and free promotions that favour open models; only the day's listed models; enterprise traffic that goes direct to the labs never appears; a model counts as closed if OpenRouter names no repository for it, including a delisted one.
description: The share of tokens routed through OpenRouter that went to models whose weights are published, among the models in OpenRouter's daily top table, the last reading in each week. A model counts as open when OpenRouter lists a Hugging Face repository for it.
name: Open models' share of routed tokens
question: Of the tokens routed through OpenRouter's most used models, what share goes to models whose weights are published?
sql:
WITH hf AS (SELECT subject, arg_max(id, as_of_date) AS hid FROM observations
            WHERE source_ns = 'openrouter' AND measure = 'hugging_face_id' GROUP BY 1),
t AS (SELECT r.as_of_date, r.id, r.value_numeric AS v, hf.hid
      FROM observations r LEFT JOIN hf ON hf.subject = r.subject
      WHERE r.source_ns = 'openrouter_rankings' AND r.measure = 'tokens' AND r.value_numeric > 0),
d AS (SELECT as_of_date, sum(CASE WHEN hid IS NOT NULL THEN v ELSE 0 END) / sum(v) AS value,
             list_concat(list(id ORDER BY id), list(hid ORDER BY hid) FILTER (WHERE hid IS NOT NULL)) AS obs_ids
      FROM t GROUP BY 1 HAVING count(*) >= 5)
SELECT * FROM d QUALIFY as_of_date = max(as_of_date) OVER (PARTITION BY date_trunc('week', as_of_date))

caveats: List prices, and an open model's price is what its hosts charge, not its makers; only models Artificial Analysis and Epoch name alike count, a minority of the open ones, old ones included; Artificial Analysis re-scores every model on its current index, so past dates use today's scores; a model it stops listing keeps its last price, so a dropped cheap model can stay the rival; at least five open models must have a closed rival; the series starts in September 2026 and records change points.
description: On each price change date, for every open model, the cheapest closed model scoring at least as high on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, its blended price (USD per million tokens, 3:1 input to output) over the open model's; the median across open models. Models are open or closed as Epoch's capability index groups them, matched by name.
name: What closed capability costs over open
question: At the same capability, how does the cheapest closed model's price compare with an open model's, typically?
sql:
WITH g AS (SELECT subject, bool_or(measure = 'eci_open') AS open, min(id) AS gid FROM observations
           WHERE source_ns = 'epoch_bench' AND measure IN ('eci_open', 'eci_closed') GROUP BY 1),
i AS (SELECT subject, arg_max(value_numeric, as_of_date) AS idx, arg_max(id, as_of_date) AS iid
      FROM observations WHERE series_key LIKE 'aa.%.intelligence_index.pt' AND value_numeric > 0 GROUP BY 1),
p AS (SELECT subject, as_of_date, value_numeric AS usd, id FROM observations
      WHERE series_key LIKE 'aa.%.price_blended_usd_per_mtok.pt' AND value_numeric > 0),
d AS (SELECT DISTINCT as_of_date FROM p),
cp AS (SELECT d.as_of_date, p.subject, arg_max(p.usd, p.as_of_date) AS usd, arg_max(p.id, p.as_of_date) AS pid
       FROM d JOIN p ON p.as_of_date <= d.as_of_date GROUP BY 1, 2),
m AS (SELECT cp.*, i.idx, i.iid, g.open, g.gid FROM cp JOIN i USING (subject) JOIN g USING (subject)),
pr AS (SELECT o.as_of_date, o.subject, o.usd, o.pid, o.iid, o.gid, list(c ORDER BY c.usd, c.subject)[1] AS rival
       FROM m o JOIN m c ON c.as_of_date = o.as_of_date AND NOT c.open AND c.idx >= o.idx
       WHERE o.open GROUP BY o.as_of_date, o.subject, o.usd, o.pid, o.iid, o.gid),
r AS (SELECT as_of_date, median(rival.usd / usd) AS value,  -- each row cited once, the grouping rows included
             list_sort(list_distinct(flatten(list([pid, iid, gid, rival.pid, rival.iid, rival.gid])))) AS obs_ids
      FROM pr GROUP BY 1 HAVING count(*) >= 5)
SELECT * FROM r QUALIFY value IS DISTINCT FROM lag(value) OVER (ORDER BY as_of_date)

caveats: Whole-company figures; filers define and disclose backlog differently, and some count only contracts over a year; fiscal quarters differ by filer; a quarter window must hold exactly four fiscal quarters.
description: Remaining performance obligations (revenue contracted but not yet delivered) at each quarter end, over revenue in the four fiscal quarters to that date, per filer, from XBRL company facts; a fiscal fourth quarter filed only inside the 10-K is the full year minus the three quarters inside it.
name: Oracle's contracted backlog
question: How many years of its current revenue has Oracle already contracted but not yet delivered?
sql:
WITH q AS (SELECT subject, as_of_date, value_numeric AS rev, [id] AS ids FROM observations
           WHERE source_ns = 'sec' AND measure = 'revenue' AND grain = 'q' AND value_numeric > 0),
fy AS (SELECT subject, as_of_date, period_start, value_numeric AS rev, id FROM observations
       WHERE source_ns = 'sec' AND measure = 'revenue' AND grain = 'fy'),
fill AS (  -- a fiscal Q4 filed only inside the 10-K: the full year minus the three quarters inside it
  SELECT f.subject, f.as_of_date, f.rev - sum(q.rev) AS rev, flatten(list_prepend([f.id], list(q.ids))) AS ids
  FROM fy f JOIN q ON q.subject = f.subject AND q.as_of_date > f.period_start AND q.as_of_date < f.as_of_date
  GROUP BY f.subject, f.as_of_date, f.rev, f.id
  HAVING count(*) = 3 AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM q q2 WHERE q2.subject = f.subject AND q2.as_of_date = f.as_of_date)),
qs AS (SELECT * FROM q UNION ALL SELECT * FROM fill),
ttm AS (  -- four quarter ends inside ten and a half months: exactly the four fiscal quarters to this date
  SELECT a.subject, a.as_of_date, sum(b.rev) AS rev, flatten(list(b.ids)) AS ids
  FROM qs a JOIN qs b ON b.subject = a.subject AND b.as_of_date <= a.as_of_date AND b.as_of_date > a.as_of_date - INTERVAL 320 DAY
  GROUP BY a.subject, a.as_of_date HAVING count(*) = 4 AND count(DISTINCT b.as_of_date) = 4)
SELECT r.as_of_date, r.subject AS entity, r.value_numeric / t.rev AS value, list_prepend(r.id, t.ids) AS obs_ids
FROM observations r JOIN ttm t ON t.subject = r.subject AND t.as_of_date = r.as_of_date
WHERE r.source_ns = 'sec' AND r.measure = 'rpo' AND r.grain = 'q' AND t.rev > 0

caveats: A floor. The ledger was searched under its written rule on 23 Sep 2026 for every buyer from 1 January 2025 (the rule, the searches and every deal considered and left out are at the head of its rows in seed/manual_observations.yaml); a quarter is read only once a sweep has covered it. Four deals met the rule but no citable page states them (three in 2025, one in 2026), so they are not counted. Acquihires surface late, so a sweep can add deals to quarters already read. Each deal counts from its earliest dated row. Undisclosed prices still count as events; deals by companies outside the buyer set (Stripe, Cloudflare, Cognition, Mercor) stay in the ledger uncounted.
description: Distinct deals in the trailing four quarters by which a buyer (an entity whose primary membership is in the model or compute layer) took a company in one of the fourteen sublayers above the model layer (training input, serving and orchestration, deployment and application), by purchase, acquihire, or a licence or stake that came with its leaders; counted from the acquisition ledger (one per acquirer-target pair) at each quarter end a sweep has covered. The ledger's written rule is at the head of its rows in seed/manual_observations.yaml; deals by anyone else stay in the ledger uncounted.
name: Labs and compute companies buying the layers above them
question: In the year to each searched quarter, how many companies in the layers above the model layer did the labs and compute companies buy, or hire the teams of?
sql:
WITH buyers AS (SELECT DISTINCT entity_id FROM entity_membership WHERE is_primary AND layer_id IN ('model', 'compute_physical')),
deals AS (
  SELECT subject || '/' || measure AS deal, min(as_of_date) AS announced, list(id ORDER BY id) AS ids
  FROM observations WHERE source_ns = 'acq' AND subject IN (SELECT entity_id FROM buyers) GROUP BY 1),
swept AS (SELECT DATE '2026-06-30' AS through),  -- the last quarter end a sweep has covered (23 Sep 2026); each sweep's PR raises it
spine AS (  -- every completed, swept calendar quarter from the ledger's start; the quarter under way is never read
  SELECT (range + INTERVAL 3 MONTH - INTERVAL 1 DAY)::DATE AS q
  FROM range(DATE '2025-01-01', least(date_trunc('quarter', current_date)::DATE, (SELECT through FROM swept) + 1), INTERVAL 3 MONTH))
SELECT s.q AS as_of_date, count(*) AS value, flatten(list(d.ids ORDER BY d.deal)) AS obs_ids
FROM spine s JOIN deals d ON d.announced <= s.q AND d.announced > s.q - INTERVAL 12 MONTH
WHERE s.q - INTERVAL 12 MONTH >= DATE '2024-12-31'
GROUP BY s.q ORDER BY s.q

caveats: OpenAI's own figures as reported by the press; subscribers and weekly users are different counts (a subscriber need not use it every week), so the ratio compares two counts and is not the share of users who pay.
description: ChatGPT's paying subscribers over its weekly active users, as OpenAI states them, on each date OpenAI states both.
name: Paying subscribers against weekly users of ChatGPT
question: What are ChatGPT's paying consumer subscribers as a share of its weekly users?
sql:
SELECT s.as_of_date, s.value_numeric / u.value_numeric AS value, [s.id, u.id] AS obs_ids
FROM observations s JOIN observations u
  ON u.as_of_date = s.as_of_date AND u.series_key = 'usage.openai_chatgpt.weekly_active_users.pt'
WHERE s.series_key = 'usage.openai_chatgpt.paying_subscribers.pt' AND u.value_numeric > 0

caveats: Hand-kept from dated public reports, so it undercounts; an event is counted once on its own date, and a court's ruling in a case already counted is context, not a second event. When the window empties, the reading cites the event that left it.
description: For each of the outlook's hand-kept event ledgers (checking AI's work sold as a category, insurers' AI exclusions, platforms fencing out outside agents), the number of events for and against in the twelve months to each date on which an event lands or one leaves the window.
name: Platforms fencing out outside agents
question: In the year to the date shown, how many times did a large platform move to keep outside AI agents off it?
sql:
WITH e AS (SELECT subject AS target, measure AS stance, as_of_date, id FROM observations
           WHERE source_ns = 'evidence' AND subject IN ('ai_evaluation_market', 'insurer_ai_exclusions', 'agent_access_fences')
             AND measure IN ('for', 'against')),
d AS (SELECT target, stance, as_of_date AS day, NULL AS gone FROM e
      UNION ALL  -- the day an event ages out of the trailing year, up to today
      SELECT target, stance, CAST(as_of_date + INTERVAL 1 YEAR AS DATE), id FROM e
      WHERE as_of_date + INTERVAL 1 YEAR <= current_date),
c AS (SELECT d.target, d.stance, d.day, count(DISTINCT e.id) AS n, list(DISTINCT e.id ORDER BY e.id) FILTER (WHERE e.id IS NOT NULL) AS ids,
             max(d.gone) AS gone
      FROM d LEFT JOIN e ON e.target = d.target AND e.stance = d.stance AND e.as_of_date <= d.day AND e.as_of_date > d.day - INTERVAL 1 YEAR
      GROUP BY 1, 2, 3)
SELECT day AS as_of_date, target, stance, n AS value, CASE WHEN n = 0 THEN [gone] ELSE ids END AS obs_ids FROM c

caveats: ADP payroll records, not the whole labour market; the spread is measured from November 2022 and moves with anything that treats young and old workers differently, not only AI.
description: Within a fifth of occupations ranked by exposure to AI, the employment index of workers aged 22 to 25 minus that of workers aged 50 and over, monthly; each index is set to 100 in November 2022, so the spread is zero there by construction (Stanford Digital Economy Lab and ADP Research). One row for the most exposed fifth and one for the least, its control.
name: Young against old workers in the most exposed jobs
question: In the jobs most exposed to AI, how far has employment of workers aged 22 to 25 fallen behind that of workers aged 50 and over since November 2022?
sql:
SELECT j.as_of_date, 'most_exposed' AS quintile, j.value_numeric - s.value_numeric AS value, [j.id, s.id] AS obs_ids
FROM observations j JOIN observations s
  ON s.as_of_date = j.as_of_date AND s.series_key = 'canaries.us_exposure_q5_age_50_plus.employment_index.m'
WHERE j.series_key = 'canaries.us_exposure_q5_age_22_25.employment_index.m'
UNION ALL
SELECT j.as_of_date, 'least_exposed', j.value_numeric - s.value_numeric, [j.id, s.id]
FROM observations j JOIN observations s
  ON s.as_of_date = j.as_of_date AND s.series_key = 'canaries.us_exposure_q1_age_50_plus.employment_index.m'
WHERE j.series_key = 'canaries.us_exposure_q1_age_22_25.employment_index.m'

caveats: One evaluator's agents, each dated by its model's release (one model can appear at two settings); a straight line through a handful of points, so one new agent can move it. HAL draws its own trend lines with the same fit.
description: How fast HAL's scores have risen across model releases, per year, as the slope of a least-squares line through every agent HAL evaluates against its model's release date; one row for accuracy and one for overall reliability, dated at the newest release. Both scores run from 0 to 1 (accuracy as a share of tasks), so the slope is in points, hundredths of that range, a year.
name: How fast agents are getting more accurate
question: Across the agents HAL evaluates, how many points a year has accuracy risen across model releases?
sql:
SELECT max(as_of_date) AS as_of_date, measure, regr_slope(value_numeric, datediff('day', DATE '2000-01-01', as_of_date)) * 365.25 AS value,
       list(id ORDER BY id) AS obs_ids
FROM observations
WHERE source_ns = 'hal_reliability' AND measure IN ('accuracy', 'reliability') AND grain = 'pt'
  AND value_numeric IS NOT NULL AND NOT coalesce(disputed, false)
GROUP BY measure HAVING count(*) >= 5

caveats: The peak is the highest quarter since this site's FRED history begins in 2015; each quarter reads the stored release of both quarters, which BEA revises, and the bet itself reads BEA's third estimate in a close call.
description: US real gross domestic product per person (BEA, quarterly, via FRED) over its previous peak, minus one, where the previous peak is the highest quarter up to and including the same quarter a year before; the measure the growth bet between Benjamin Moll, Alex Imas and others reads.
name: Output per person over its previous peak
question: How far does American real output per person stand above the highest level it reached a year or more before, the reading the growth bet settles on?
sql:
WITH q AS (SELECT as_of_date, value_numeric AS v, id FROM observations WHERE series_key = 'fred.us.real_gdp_per_capita.q'),
p AS (SELECT as_of_date, v, id,
             max(v) OVER w AS peak, arg_max(id, v) OVER w AS peak_id
      FROM q WINDOW w AS (ORDER BY as_of_date RANGE BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND INTERVAL 1 YEAR PRECEDING))
SELECT as_of_date, v / peak - 1 AS value, [id, peak_id] AS obs_ids FROM p WHERE peak IS NOT NULL

caveats: An official statistic, revised as its agency revises it; the year-on-year change reads the stored release of both ends.
description: US real output per person, year on year, from FRED (quarterly, BEA).
name: Output per person, year on year
question: How fast is American real output per person growing on a year before?
sql:
SELECT a.as_of_date, a.value_numeric / b.value_numeric - 1 AS value, [a.id, b.id] AS obs_ids
FROM observations a JOIN observations b ON b.series_key = a.series_key AND b.period_start = a.period_start - INTERVAL 12 MONTH
WHERE a.series_key = 'fred.us.real_gdp_per_capita.q' AND b.value_numeric > 0

caveats: Epoch's estimates, not verified builds: it states power within a factor of 1.4 and dates within six months, and covers roughly half of capacity, mostly the largest sites. 'Built' means dated on or before today; 'planned' means dated after it. A finished site leaves the comparison, so the ratio does not drift toward one with the calendar. A fast build-out with no shortage would read the same. Dated by the day Epoch's file last changed in our ledger; a revision that only removes rows does not advance it. The calendar moves the value under that date as well: a milestone Epoch projected counts as built once its date passes, whether or not Epoch has confirmed it, and a site with no later milestone leaves the comparison. No reading when fewer than twenty sites compare, because one campus could then carry the ratio.
description: Across the AI data-centre sites Epoch tracks that have both figures: the sum of each site's largest planned power divided by the sum of each site's newest built power. `sites: all` keeps sites where nothing is built yet; `sites: built` leaves them out.
name: Planned against built data-centre power
question: How far does the power Epoch expects at the sites it tracks run ahead of what is built there?
sql:
WITH s AS (SELECT 'all' AS sites, * FROM dc_sites UNION ALL SELECT 'built', * FROM dc_sites WHERE built_mw > 0)
SELECT any_value(read_on) AS as_of_date, sites, sum(planned_mw) / sum(built_mw) AS value,
       list_sort(list_concat(list(built_id), list(planned_id))) AS obs_ids
FROM s GROUP BY sites HAVING count(*) >= 20 AND sum(built_mw) > 0

caveats: Same dating and definitions as dc_projected_to_observed_power.
description: How many data-centre sites stand behind dc_projected_to_observed_power: `sites: all` is every site with both a built and a planned figure; `sites: unbuilt` is those among them where nothing is built yet.
name: Sites behind the data-centre gap
question: How many sites carry both a built and a planned figure, and how many of them are still bare?
sql:
WITH s AS (SELECT 'all' AS sites, * FROM dc_sites UNION ALL SELECT 'unbuilt', * FROM dc_sites WHERE built_mw = 0)
SELECT any_value(read_on) AS as_of_date, sites, count(*) AS value,
       list_sort(list_concat(list(built_id), list(planned_id))) AS obs_ids
FROM s GROUP BY sites

caveats: Memory supply is published in dollars, so a price rise reads as a supply rise. Supply alone says nothing about demand. Epoch's estimates, which it says are firmer by year than by quarter.
description: Growth over twelve months in the quarterly supply of each input AI chips consume: advanced packaging and leading-edge logic in wafers, high-bandwidth memory in dollars. A fraction: 0.5 is up by half.

question: How fast is the supply of packaging, leading-edge logic and high-bandwidth memory growing?
sql:
SELECT a.as_of_date, a.measure AS input, a.value_numeric / b.value_numeric - 1 AS value, [a.id, b.id] AS obs_ids
FROM observations a JOIN observations b
  ON b.series_key = a.series_key AND b.as_of_date = a.as_of_date - INTERVAL 12 MONTH
WHERE a.source_ns = 'epoch_components' AND a.subject = 'global' AND b.value_numeric > 0
  AND NOT coalesce(a.disputed, false) AND NOT coalesce(b.disputed, false)

caveats: Epoch's 'Other' bucket is counted as one buyer though it is many, which overstates the index a little: treating it as many small buyers gives about 0.37, leaving it out about 0.52, against 0.39 here (last quarter of 2025). Epoch's estimates; medians only.
description: Concentration among the buyers of advanced chip packaging (TSMC's CoWoS): the Herfindahl index over each designer's share of packaging supply, per quarter, on a full panel.
name: Who buys advanced packaging
question: How concentrated are the buyers of advanced chip packaging?
sql:
WITH x AS (SELECT subject, as_of_date, value_numeric AS v, id FROM observations
           WHERE source_ns = 'epoch_components' AND measure = 'cowos_share_pct' AND NOT coalesce(disputed, false)),
first AS (SELECT subject, min(as_of_date) AS f FROM x GROUP BY 1),
need AS (SELECT d.as_of_date, count(*) AS n FROM (SELECT DISTINCT as_of_date FROM x) d JOIN first ON first.f <= d.as_of_date GROUP BY 1),
have AS (SELECT as_of_date, count(*) AS n, sum(v) AS tot, list(id ORDER BY id) AS ids FROM x GROUP BY 1),
panel AS (SELECT have.* FROM have JOIN need USING (as_of_date) WHERE have.n = need.n AND have.n >= 3)
SELECT p.as_of_date, sum((x.v / p.tot) * (x.v / p.tot)) AS value, p.ids AS obs_ids
FROM panel p JOIN x USING (as_of_date) GROUP BY p.as_of_date, p.ids

caveats: A stock of chips sold to date, not the flow of new sales, so it moves slowly. Epoch's estimates. The newest full panel lags the newest partial one by up to three quarters.
description: Concentration of AI chip supply by designer: the Herfindahl index (sum of squared shares) over each designer's cumulative chip sales in H100-equivalents, on each quarter end where every designer that has started reporting is present.
name: Concentration of AI chip supply

caveats: Demand only: the power chips would draw, not the power the grid can supply. Rated draw of chips sold, whether or not they are switched on. Epoch's estimates.
description: Growth over twelve months in the power drawn by all AI chips sold to date (megawatts, summed across designers), on quarter ends where the same full panel of designers reported on both dates. A fraction: 1.0 is a doubling.
name: Power drawn by the chip fleet
question: How fast is the electricity the installed AI chips would draw growing?
sql:
WITH x AS (SELECT subject, as_of_date, value_numeric AS v, id FROM observations
           WHERE source_ns = 'epoch_chips' AND measure = 'power_mw_cumulative' AND NOT coalesce(disputed, false)),
first AS (SELECT subject, min(as_of_date) AS f FROM x GROUP BY 1),
need AS (SELECT d.as_of_date, count(*) AS n FROM (SELECT DISTINCT as_of_date FROM x) d JOIN first ON first.f <= d.as_of_date GROUP BY 1),
have AS (SELECT as_of_date, count(*) AS n, sum(v) AS tot, list(id ORDER BY id) AS ids FROM x GROUP BY 1),
panel AS (SELECT have.* FROM have JOIN need USING (as_of_date) WHERE have.n = need.n AND have.n >= 3)
SELECT a.as_of_date, a.tot / b.tot - 1 AS value, list_concat(a.ids, b.ids) AS obs_ids
FROM panel a JOIN panel b ON b.as_of_date = a.as_of_date - INTERVAL 12 MONTH AND b.n = a.n

caveats: A trend since 2012, so it is slow to show a stall. Only accelerators with a public release price; recent data-centre GPUs have none, so the series may end well before today.
description: Yearly change in the release price of a unit of accelerator compute (dollars per FP16 FLOP per second), from a log-linear fit across chips by release date. A fraction: -0.2 is twenty percent cheaper each year.

caveats: The basket is editorial: flagship families by name, with small tiers (nano, mini, lite, flash, haiku and the like) and image, experimental and tool-tuned builds left out, and it ages as families turn over. List prices on one router, from the six vendors the connector keeps. One cheap model sets the minimum. A delisted model keeps its last price, because the ledger holds price changes and has no last-seen date.
description: The cheapest output price, in dollars per million tokens, among a named basket of flagship models on OpenRouter, each model's latest price carried forward, on each date a price changed.
name: Cheapest model in the flagship basket
question: What does the cheapest capable model cost to run?
sql:
WITH p AS (
  SELECT subject, as_of_date, value_numeric AS usd, id, split_part(raw_snippet, ' ', 1) AS model
  FROM observations WHERE source_ns = 'openrouter' AND measure = 'price_completion_usd_per_mtok' AND value_numeric > 0),
basket AS (
  SELECT * FROM p
  WHERE regexp_matches(model, '^(openai/(gpt-5|gpt-6|o3)|anthropic/claude-(opus|sonnet|fable)|google/gemini-(2\.5-pro|3)|x-ai/grok-4|deepseek/deepseek-(r1|v3|v4))')
    AND NOT contains(model, ':')  -- router variants (:free, :batch); the connector drops them today
    AND NOT regexp_matches(split_part(model, '/', 2), '(^|[-_.])(nano|mini|lite|flash|haiku|small|tiny|8b|4b|distill|image|exp|customtools)([-_.]|$)')),
d AS (SELECT DISTINCT as_of_date FROM basket),
cp AS (SELECT d.as_of_date, b.subject, arg_max(b.usd, b.as_of_date) AS usd, arg_max(b.id, b.as_of_date) AS pid
       FROM d JOIN basket b ON b.as_of_date <= d.as_of_date GROUP BY 1, 2),
r AS (SELECT as_of_date, min(usd) AS value, [arg_min(pid, (usd, pid))] AS obs_ids FROM cp GROUP BY as_of_date)  -- a tie cites the lowest id, every run
SELECT * FROM r QUALIFY value IS DISTINCT FROM lag(value) OVER (ORDER BY as_of_date)  -- change points only

caveats: Not all of this spending is for AI. A trailing total turns about two quarters after a single quarter would. Quarters are differenced from year-to-date filings exactly as in capex_to_revenue_stack.
description: Growth over twelve months in the trailing four quarters of capital spending by Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon, Meta and Oracle (filed), at each quarter end. A fraction: 0.5 is up by half.

question: Are the five largest builders still raising their spending?
sql:
SELECT (a.cq + INTERVAL 3 MONTH - INTERVAL 1 DAY)::DATE AS as_of_date, a.v / b.v - 1 AS value,
       list_distinct(list_concat(a.ids, b.ids)) AS obs_ids
FROM hyperscaler_capex_ttm a JOIN hyperscaler_capex_ttm b ON b.cq = a.cq - INTERVAL 12 MONTH
